title: Level 4 (Expert) - B-10
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 4♥. After winning the spade opening lead in dummy, South must try to draw trump without allowing East to gain the lead. East may be able to play diamonds through the ♦K, allowing the defense to take 3 diamond tricks.

South does not mind losing a trump trick as long as West wins that trick. South should lead a heart from dummy at trick 2. When East follows with the ♥5, South should play small from his hand. West can win cheaply, but the contract is safe unless West has 4 hearts (in which case South's choice of plays does not matter).

South wins the spade return and cashes a top heart honour. If both defenders follow, South can draw the last trump and run the clubs for a diamond discard. If West discards on the second round of trump, South can cross in clubs and finesse against the ♥Q. South can draw the last trump and run the clubs for a diamond discard.

If East follows with a middle heart (or the ♥Q) on the first round of trump, South should win the ♥A or ♥K. South has plenty of dummy entries to pick up East's trump holding by finessing two more times.
